{{short description|Mathematical concept}}
{{one source |date=April 2024}}
A '''discontinuous group''' is a mathematical concept relating to mappings in [[topological space]].

==Definition==
Let <math>T</math> be a topological space of points <math>\tau</math>, and let <math>\tau\to f(\tau,x)</math>, <math>x\in G</math>, be an open continuous representation of the [[topological group]] <math>G</math> as a [[transitive relation|transitive]] group of [[homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] mappings of <math>T</math> on itself. The representation <math>\tau\to f(\tau,a)</math> <math>a\in H</math> of the discrete subgroup <math>H\sub G</math> in <math>T</math> is called discontinuous, if no sequence <math>f(\tau,a_n)</math> (<math>n=1,2,\ldots</math>) converges to a point in <math>T</math>, as <math>a_n</math> runs over distinct elements of <math>H</math>.<ref>{{citation|surname1=Carl Ludwig Siegel|editor-surname1= Annals of Mathematics|title=Discontinuous groups|volume=44|issue=4|at=pp.&nbsp;674−689|date=1943
}}</ref>
